note: Curated single-style system for collage-poster: contemporary editorial photo-collage — greyscale photographic fragments plus at most two FLAT spot colours, on near-white paper, with torn/taped edges, a faint modular grid, register marks, and mono edge annotations. This is ONE style explored across parametric dimensions so it reproduces reliably across subjects. SKILL.md prose explains intent; when a value conflicts, this file wins.

social_story.use_for: IG / TikTok story & reel, full-screen vertical

substack_cover.note: Substack's recommended featured/cover image size — 14:10 aspect ratio, per Substack's 2026 image-size guidance.

ratios.note: Offer ratio as a choice at the Steering step EVERY time (portrait / social / landscape / Substack presets), not only when missing. The composition adapts to the ratio: landscape (16:9, 1.91:1, Substack ~1.4:1) spreads the collage horizontally, rebalances the anchor/diagonal, and moves the headline to a side rather than stacking; square centres the stack; 9:16 stacks fragments vertically with more breathing top and bottom; 4:5 is a gentle portrait crop of 3:4.

defaults.note: Deterministic: same brief resolves the same look. The greyscale photographic base is constant; only the spot palette, composition and element mix vary.

greyscale_base.note: The photographic collage is ALWAYS greyscale charcoal — this is the constant of the style. Spot colours are separate flat shapes; they never tint the photos.

spot_rules: At most TWO spot colours, always as FLAT shapes (circles, bands, blocks) — never as a tint on the photographs.
The photographs stay greyscale; colour lives only in the flat spot shapes and, optionally, one small element that keeps its natural colour if it ties to a spot.
Spots sit behind or beside the greyscale fragments, not over the whole page.

elements.name: Torn Photo Fragment
elements.role: the subject, as a greyscale cut-out with a torn or rough edge

elements.name: Taped Strip
elements.role: a strip of photo or paper that looks taped down

elements.name: Diagonal Photo Slab
elements.role: a long rectangular photo band crossing the composition on a diagonal

elements.name: Flat Spot Circle
elements.role: a flat circle in a spot colour sitting behind fragments

elements.name: Flat Spot Band
elements.role: a flat rectangle/band in a spot colour

elements.name: Faint Grid
elements.role: a very light modular grid or small grid squares under the collage

elements.name: Register Marks
elements.role: small 'x' marks or crop corners, print-shop feel

elements.name: Outline Rectangle
elements.role: a thin unfilled rectangle framing or offsetting an element

elements.name: Page Number
elements.role: a large index/page-style number, usually a corner

elements.name: Rotated Edge Text
elements.role: small mono text set vertically along a side edge
elements.note: generic label only — never a real brand/handle/URL

compositions.title_relation: big display anchored to a bottom corner; small labels orbit the stack
compositions.note: fragments overlap in a central vertical band

compositions.title_relation: headline meets or is crossed by the diagonal slab
compositions.note: one photo slab cuts across the subject

compositions.title_relation: labels and dates scatter to the margins; one big display at an edge
compositions.note: fragments and spots spread with intentional white gaps

display_voices.name: Condensed Grotesk
display_voices.desc: bold condensed or compressed grotesk, uppercase

display_voices.name: High-contrast Serif Display
display_voices.desc: high-contrast display serif, roman or italic

typography.display: one display voice chosen from display_voices at the Steering step (default condensed_grotesk), uppercase; the headline anchors a corner or crosses a fragment
typography.support: small monospaced or plain grotesk — see `annotations`
typography.orientation: one orientation event max — the rotated vertical edge text is the usual one
typography.note: One display voice per poster, chosen at Steering; never mix two display faces.

annotations.note: Page number, dates, index and edge label are DECIDED at the Steering step, not left to chance — the image model would otherwise invent values every run (this is why they vary between generations). The user sets exact values, asks for model-invented generic marks, or turns them off.
annotations.discipline: When invented, they are GENERIC editorial marks only — never a real brand, @handle, URL, or a date presented as a real event.

treatment: greyscale photographic collage — torn photo fragments, taped strips, overlapping layers, subtle photocopy grain and print texture; flat spot shapes behind
texture: photocopy/print grain, torn and taped edges, faint grid lines, register marks, slight analog imperfection
rules: Photographs are greyscale only; colour lives in at most two flat spot shapes.
Keep 35-50% of the page as breathing white/paper — the collage is dense but the margins are calm.
One diagonal or orientation event, not several competing angles.
A faint grid plus a few register marks give the analog print feel — do not overfill with marks.
All annotations (dates, index, edge text, page number) are GENERIC editorial marks — never a real brand, handle, or URL, and never invented as if factual.

Real-world objects (cars, street signs, storefronts, packaging) must not show real logos, brand badges, license plates, or readable trademarks — keep them generic, plain, or obscured. Image models leak these; add them to the negatives every time.
Torn/taped edges and grain carry the handmade feel; avoid glossy clean vector flatness.
